citation: Wang, Ruijie, Yuanchen Xu, and Liming Chen. "GazeMotive: A Gaze-Based Motivation-Aware E-Learning Tool for Students with Learning Difficulties." In D. Lamas et al. (eds.), INTERACT 2019, LNCS 11749, pp. 544-548. Springer Nature Switzerland AG, 2019. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-29390-1_34.
discipline: user modeling and personalisation for assistive learning technology (HCI, e-learning), demonstrating a gaze-based motivation-assessment tool
thesis: GazeMotive is a working Windows-desktop demonstration of applying eye tracking to real-time motivation assessment in an e-learning environment for students with learning difficulties. It introduces no new motivation theory or validation study; it implements a motivation model and gaze-based prediction models the same author group already developed and validated in earlier work (refs [1], [2], [5]): a Tobii eye tracker records gaze during learning, gaze features (average pupil diameter, fixation number over Areas of Interest) plus self-reported data feed previously-built logistic regression models to infer motivational states (e.g., Self-Efficacy, Visual Attractiveness, Reading Experience, Confirmed Fit, Attitudes Toward School), and a pedagogical agent delivers personalised text/picture feedback intended to sustain or enhance motivation and engagement in real time. Boredom is never named in the extracted text; the paper's own vocabulary is uniformly motivation and engagement, with disengagement gestured at only indirectly via 'dropouts' and 'low levels of engagement' among students with learning difficulties.

sections.title: Abstract/keywords
sections.summary: States the system, its Tobii-tracker-plus-pedagogical-agent architecture, and its aim of motivation-enhanced learning; keywords: eye tracking, motivation assessment, personalised feedback.

sections.title: 1 Introduction -- 1.1 Background
sections.summary: Motivates personalised learning for students with learning difficulties (dyslexia); argues prior assistive-learning personalisation research has targeted learners' emotion and cognition (inducing positive emotion, reattracting attention) but neglected motivation specifically.

sections.title: 1.2 Motivation Assessment
sections.summary: Summarises the previously developed multi-factor motivation model (intrinsic motivation e.g. Self-Efficacy, extrinsic motivation e.g. Visual Attractiveness, mediators e.g. Reading Experience) and the prior gaze-based prediction study (ref [5]: average pupil diameter and fixation number, accuracy up to 81.3%).

sections.title: 1.3 The Demonstration System
sections.summary: Describes how gaze features (via AOIs) and self-report inputs feed the existing logistic-regression models to assess distinct motivational factors, some purely from gaze (Confirmed Fit, Reading Experience), others from self-report (Attitudes Toward School, Self-Efficacy).

sections.title: 2 GazeMotive Walkthrough
sections.summary: Expert interface: login, adding/deleting learning materials and quizzes, marking Areas of Interest (AOIs) by clicking polygon corners (Fig.1). Learner interface: pedagogical-agent feedback in text/picture form triggered by motivational-state detection during learning pages and quizzes (Fig.2).

sections.title: 3 Conclusion
sections.summary: Restates the demonstration's contribution (applying the motivation model and personalisation rules to a real-world scenario via gaze); names future work: continued model/algorithm validation, improved interface design, more motivational dimensions, more diverse feedback formats (speech, animation).

sections.title: References
sections.summary: 7 items: five are the authors' own prior/companion work (motivation model development, gaze-based prediction study); two are external (eye-tracking-in-HCI survey; eye-activity-as-emotion-indicator study), plus two non-scholarly sources (course materials, design-guidance blog).

constructs.label: flow / engagement (contrast pole)
constructs.treatment: the paper's real organizing construct: the system exists to detect and remediate low motivation/engagement and sustain 'motivation-enhanced learning experience and better learning performance'; 'motivation and engagement' are named together as the target outcome

constructs.label: attentional disengagement / meta-awareness
constructs.treatment: treated only indirectly, via two gaze-detected proxies rather than the paper's own vocabulary: a 'negative reading experience' flagged during a learning page, and a user detected as 'having not put enough effort' during a quiz -- functional stand-ins for disengagement, not the paper's own theorized construct (P/anticipatory-application for the mapping)

constructs.label: situational vs. trait/state boredom
constructs.treatment: not treated as boredom, but the motivation model draws a parallel stability split: Self-Efficacy and Attitudes Toward School are trait-like ('usually remain stable in a short-term period'), assessed once via self-report; Confirmed Fit and Reading Experience vary dynamically, assessed continuously from gaze -- a motivation-domain analogue, not a boredom-domain claim

constructs.label: boredom proneness / mind-wandering-task-unrelated-thought / monotony-meaninglessness / temporality of boredom / boredom-as-regulatory-signal / profound-deep boredom / being-bored-by / being-bored-with
constructs.treatment: none treated; no phenomenological or boredom-specific vocabulary appears anywhere in the extracted text

measures.label: gaze variance / fixation dispersion
measures.signal: AOI-based gaze features, including fixation number, computed per learning-material page over expert-marked Areas of Interest
measures.sampleN: not reported in this demonstration paper; the underlying prediction accuracy and sample belong to the cited prior study (ref [5])
measures.keyResult: no new accuracy figure reported here; ref [5]'s prior experiment reported up to 81.3% prediction accuracy using fixation number and pupil diameter

measures.label: pupil dilation / pupillometry
measures.sampleN: not reported in this paper; cited from ref [5]'s prior experiment with students with learning difficulties
measures.keyResult: cited as one of two gaze features (with fixation number) found to play a significant role in motivation assessment, contributing to ref [5]'s 81.3% accuracy

measures.label: self-report / survey scale
measures.signal: self-input data collected at session start (for stable intrinsic-motivation factors: Attitudes Toward School, Self-Efficacy) plus the multi-item questionnaire study underlying the original motivation model
measures.apparatus: in-application self-input form; prior multi-item questionnaire instrument (refs [1],[2])
measures.sampleN: not reported in this paper for the demo system; questionnaire-study N belongs to refs [1]/[2], not extracted
measures.keyResult: no accuracy/validity figure reported for self-report inputs in this paper; used to assess factors treated as short-term stable rather than dynamically varying

measures.label: ML classification
measures.signal: logistic regression models predicting motivational-factor states from gaze features
measures.apparatus: previously-built logistic regression models (ref [5]), reused and feature-pruned ('improved... by including only the gaze features that have significant prediction power')
measures.sampleN: not reported in this paper; belongs to ref [5]
measures.keyResult: no new accuracy reported in this demonstration; ref [5]'s original models achieved up to 81.3% prediction accuracy

measures.label: behavioral (RT / errors / performance-monitoring)
measures.apparatus: in-application quiz module, combined with real-time gaze data
measures.keyResult: an incorrect quiz answer co-occurring with gaze-detected low effort triggers a specific motivational-feedback message; no aggregate statistic reported

readings.claim: The system implements the prior motivation model and prediction models inside a working expert/learner-interface application, using Tobii 4c gaze plus self-report to assess motivational factors and trigger real-time personalised feedback.
The 81.3% gaze-based motivation-prediction accuracy is a cited result from the authors' own prior study (ref [5]), not a finding newly generated in this demonstration paper.

Two concrete feedback triggers are shown: detection of a 'negative reading experience' from gaze during a learning page, and detection of a user having 'not put enough effort' from gaze co-occurring with an incorrect quiz answer.

Stated future work: continued validation of the models/algorithms to maximise assessment/feedback accuracy, improved interface design, more motivational dimensions, and more diverse feedback formats (speech, animation).
No statistical results, effect sizes, or new sample are reported for GazeMotive itself; all quantitative claims trace to the cited companion study (ref [5]).

tensions.note: GazeMotive presents itself as a working application built on already-validated models, but reports no new accuracy figure, sample, or statistical result of its own; all quantitative motivation-prediction claims (81.3% accuracy) trace to the cited companion study (ref [5]), a distinction this entry treats as load-bearing for how the paper should be cited.

the motivation model itself splits factors by presumed short-term stability (Self-Efficacy, Attitudes Toward School assessed once via self-report) versus dynamic variability (Confirmed Fit, Reading Experience assessed continuously via gaze) -- a motivation-domain parallel to the boredom field's trait/state distinction, not itself a boredom claim.

dataset_channels.target: Boredom Experiment (VR Attention Study) -- gaze-based motivation/engagement channel
dataset_channels.note: GazeMotive's AOI-plus-average-pupil-diameter-plus-fixation-number feature set, and its trait/state-like split between self-report- and gaze-assessed motivational factors, sketch a plausible template for a future VR attention study's engagement/motivation channel, but a VR headset's integrated eye tracking would differ substantially in geometry (3D gaze vectors, headset-relative AOIs) from this study's screen-based Tobii 4C setup; linkage requires the dataset entry's own instrumentation to be confirmed (P/anticipatory-application).
